back: The tools as the model sees them: names, descriptions, inputs and results. Design it for the model, as you would a screen for a person.
It tells the model what the tool does and when to use it. The model reads it on every call, so vague words cost calls.
front: What is a tool description for?

back: It names what went wrong and what to do next, in a few words. A bare 'Invalid input' leaves the model guessing.
A tool that does not change its environment. A read-only hint says so, and a hint is not a check.
A tool that may change or delete things. Treat its call as a decision, not a read.
When neither writes a resource the other reads or writes. A read and an edit of the same file are not.
front: When are two tool calls parallel-safe?

back: The tools wire: the definitions are sent with every call.
front: On which wire does a tool description sit?

back: A hint a tool server gives about a tool. Clients should not make tool-use decisions on untrusted annotations.
